ai.literal: The undiminishing lamp called family, when the soot called laziness spreads over it, will be extinguished and ruined.
ai.translation: The never-failing lamp of one's family lineage will flicker out and die when the soot of laziness spreads over it.
ai.modern: குடும்பம் என்னும் குறையாத விளக்கு, சோம்பல் என்னும் கரி படிந்து பரவுவதால் அணைந்து அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid visual metaphor to warn against the dangers of laziness. A family's honor, prosperity, and lineage are compared to a bright, undiminishing lamp (விளக்கம்). Laziness (மடி) is compared to dark soot (மாசு) that gradually crawls and spreads (ஊர) over the lamp. If laziness is allowed to take over, it smothers the flame, causing the family's light to be extinguished (மாய்ந்து) and completely ruined (கெடும்).

ai.literal: Sloth destroying, conducting oneself, family as an exalted family, those who desire.
ai.translation: Those who desire to elevate their family to an exalted status must live their lives by destroying laziness.
ai.modern: தங்கள் குடும்பத்தை உயர்ந்த குடியாக உயர்த்த விரும்புகின்றவர்கள், சோம்பலை அழித்து வாழ வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the direct link between overcoming laziness and elevating one's family status. The author uses the word 'madi' twice in the first line with different meanings: first as a noun meaning 'sloth' (madiyai) and then as a verb meaning 'destroying' (madiyā). To make one's family a noble and prosperous one (kuṭiyāka), one must actively eliminate laziness from daily conduct (oḻukal). The verse teaches that family honor is not merely inherited but must be actively built and sustained through diligent effort.

ai.literal: Sloth holding-onto-sloth lives fool born family will-perish than-himself earlier.
ai.translation: The family of the fool who lives cherishing laziness will perish even before he himself does.
ai.modern: சோம்பலைத் தன் வாழ்க்கையாகக் கொண்டு வாழ்கின்ற அறிவிலி பிறந்த குடியானது, அவனுக்கு முன்பாகவே அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive nature of laziness. It states that if a foolish person conducts his life holding onto sloth as a constant companion, the family or lineage into which he was born will be ruined first. The ruin of his household and family status will happen even before his own personal physical or moral demise. The repetition of the word 'madi' (sloth/ruin) emphasizes how laziness directly leads to destruction.

ai.literal: Family having perished, faults will increase, for those who are immersed in laziness and are without noble effort.
ai.translation: For those who are deeply immersed in laziness and lack noble effort, their family lineage will perish and their faults will multiply.
ai.modern: சோம்பலில் மூழ்கி, சிறந்த முயற்சி இல்லாதவர்களுடைய குடும்பம் அழிந்து, அவர்களின் குற்றங்கள் பெருகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the severe consequences of laziness and lack of effort. For individuals who are deeply sunk in sloth ('madi matintu') and do not possess noble exertion ('manda unatru'), two disasters occur: their family lineage ('kuti') falls into ruin, and their personal faults and vices ('kutram') multiply. The poet emphasizes that laziness is not just a passive state but an active force of destruction that ruins both one's heritage and character.

ai.literal: Procrastination, forgetfulness, laziness, and sleep, all these four, are the fondly desired vessels of those whose nature is to be ruined.
ai.translation: Procrastination, forgetfulness, laziness, and excessive sleep—these four are the cherished vessels ridden by those destined for ruin.
ai.modern: காலம் தாழ்த்துதல், மறதி, சோம்பல், அதிகத் தூக்கம் ஆகிய இந்த நான்கும் அழியும் இயல்புடையவர்கள் விரும்பி ஏறும் தோணிகளாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against four destructive habits: procrastination (நெடுநீர்), forgetfulness (மறவி), laziness (மடி), and excessive sleep (துயில்). The poet metaphorically describes these four traits as 'kāmak kalan' (fondly desired vessels or boats). Those who are destined for ruin (keṭunīrār) willingly board and cling to these habits, which act as vessels carrying them swiftly toward their own destruction. The word 'neṭunīr' literally means 'long water' but is used here to denote the habit of delaying things or dragging them out.

ai.literal: Even when the support of those who possess the earth is obtained, for those who possess laziness, attaining great benefits is rare.
ai.translation: Even if they secure the support of the rulers of the earth, those who are lazy will find it impossible to attain great benefits.
ai.modern: உலகத்தை ஆளுபவர்களின் ஆதரவைப் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், சோம்பல் உடையவர்கள் சிறந்த நன்மைகளை அடைவது அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how laziness completely neutralizes even the greatest external advantages. The word 'படி' refers to the earth, and 'படியுடையார்' means the rulers of the earth, representing the highest possible source of power and support. 'பற்று' denotes support or alliance. The poet argues that even if a person secures the backing of such powerful rulers, they cannot achieve any great or lasting benefits ('மாண்பயன்') if they are plagued by laziness ('மடி'). Ultimately, personal effort and activity are indispensable, and no amount of external patronage can compensate for sloth.

ai.literal: Desiring rebuke, scornful words they will hear, desiring laziness, excellent effort those who lack.
ai.translation: Those who embrace laziness and lack noble effort will have to endure words of rebuke and mockery from others.
ai.modern: சோம்பலை விரும்பி ஏற்று, சிறந்த முயற்சியை மேற்கொள்ளாதவர்கள், பிறர் இடித்துரைக்கும் ஏளனச் சொற்களைக் கேட்க நேரிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the social humiliation that comes with laziness. Those who choose sloth over noble, active effort lose their self-respect and standing. Consequently, they are forced to listen to harsh rebukes and mocking words from others. The poet contrasts the active pursuit of laziness with the lack of noble effort to show how inaction invites public shame.

ai.literal: If laziness dwells in one's noble family, it will surely thrust one into slavery to one's own enemies.
ai.translation: If laziness takes root in a person of noble birth, it will drag them down and force them into servitude under their enemies.
ai.modern: சோம்பல் ஒருவனுடைய உயர்ந்த குடும்பப் பெருமையில் வந்து தங்கிவிட்டால், அது அவனை அவனுடைய பகைவர்களிடம் அடிமையாகச் சேர்த்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the devastating impact of laziness on a person's social standing. Even if someone is born into an illustrious or noble family (குடிமை), allowing laziness (மடிமை) to dwell within them will destroy their status. It strips away their independence and eventually forces them into a state of servitude (அடிமை) to their adversaries (ஒன்னார்). The poet emphasizes that sloth is not just a passive flaw, but an active force that actively drives a person to ruin.

ai.literal: The faults that entered into the dignity of one's family will perish when a person dispels the dominance of laziness.
ai.translation: The blemishes that have crept into the dignity of a person's family will vanish the moment they overcome the dominance of laziness.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் சோம்பேறித்தனத்தின் ஆதிக்கத்தை ஒழித்தால், அவனுடைய குடும்பப் பெருமையில் வந்து சேர்ந்துள்ள குற்றங்கள் நீங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how laziness ruins family status and how overcoming it restores honor. The word 'குடியாண்மை' refers to the dignity, leadership, or governance of one's family line, which can be stained by faults ('குற்றம்') over time. The poet uses 'மடியாண்மை' (the rule or dominance of laziness) to describe how sloth can take complete control of a person. When a person actively dispels ('மாற்ற') this dominance of laziness, all the accumulated blemishes and decline in their family's status will completely disappear ('கெடும்').

ai.literal: A king without laziness will attain all that was spanned by the one who measured with his feet, entirely.
ai.translation: A ruler free from laziness will attain all the realms spanned by the one who measured the universe with his feet, all at once.
ai.modern: சோம்பல் இல்லாத அரசன், தன் அடியால் உலகத்தை அளந்தவன் கடந்த நிலப்பரப்பு முழுவதையும் ஒன்றாக அடைவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of overcoming laziness by comparing the rewards of an active ruler to the entire universe. The poet uses the imagery of the cosmic giant who measured the universe with his feet to represent the vastness of the earth. A king who is completely free from sloth will easily conquer and rule over all these vast territories together. The contrast highlights how diligence can overcome any boundary and bring supreme success.
